summary: In the Construct, Morpheus clicks off the television and, when Neo asks what the Matrix is, answers 'Control.' He opens the remote and defines the Matrix as 'a computer-generated dreamworld built to keep us under control in order to change a human being into this,' holding up a coppertop battery to show what humans have become. Neo rejects it — 'No! I don't believe it! It's not possible!' — and Morpheus replies that he only promised the truth, not ease. Overwhelmed, Neo demands out: 'Stop! Let me out! I want out!'

what_changes.before: He has not been told plainly what the Matrix is or what humans are used for.
what_changes.after: He is confronted with the claim that the Matrix is 'a computer-generated dreamworld built to keep us under control' and that humans are reduced to a power source, symbolized by the coppertop battery.
what_changes.evidence: The Matrix is a computer-generated dreamworld built to keep us under control in order to change a human being into this.

what_changes.before: He is trying to absorb the explanation and denies it: 'No! I don't believe it! It's not possible!'
what_changes.after: His resistance collapses into a demand to escape: 'Stop! Let me out! I want out!'
what_changes.evidence: Stop! Let me out! I want out!

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus reveals the true nature of the Matrix, and Neo recoils in denial.
